sampleSqlQueries.title: AgentSQL: Schema-Aware Agentic Text-to-SQL & MCP Server Integration (Trida Labs)
sampleSqlQueries.description: Model Context Protocol (MCP) server handler translating natural language queries into production-grade, syntax-verified SQL with schema-aware guardrails and deterministic validation
sampleSqlQueries.code:
import mcp.server.stdio
from trida.agentsql import GuardrailEngine, SchemaContext
from trida.database import SnowflakeConnector, PostgresConnector

# Initialize MCP Server for enterprise client database inspection
mcp_server = mcp.server.Server("trida-agentsql-mcp")
schema_ctx = SchemaContext.load_catalog(database="ENTERPRISE_ANALYTICS_DW")
guardrails = GuardrailEngine(strict_mode=True, max_join_depth=4)

@mcp_server.call_tool()
async def generate_production_sql(natural_query: str, client_db_target: str) -> dict:
    """
    Translates business stakeholder natural queries into production-grade,
    syntax-verified SQL with schema-aware guardrails and deterministic validation.
    """
    # 1. Extract context-aware schema embeddings
    relevant_tables = schema_ctx.resolve_semantic_entities(natural_query)
    
    # 2. Synthesize SQL with LLM contextual prompt pipeline
    raw_sql = await guardrails.synthesize_query(
        prompt=natural_query, 
        schema_metadata=relevant_tables
    )
    
    # 3. Deterministic relational integrity and RBAC verification
    validated_sql = guardrails.verify_relational_integrity(
        sql=raw_sql,
        enforce_multi_tenant_rbac=True,
        allowed_tables=["orders", "transactions", "customers", "settlements"]
    )
    
    return {
        "status": "VALIDATED_99_PCT_ACCURACY",
        "sql": validated_sql,
        "execution_target": client_db_target,
        "guardrail_checks": ["SYNTAX_VALID", "RBAC_PASSED", "NO_CARTESIAN_PRODUCT"]
    }

sampleSqlQueries.title: Data Quality Anomaly Audit Query (AWS Redshift / Athena - Global Payments)
sampleSqlQueries.description: Detects schema drift and validates null percentage across high-throughput transaction pipelines to maintain PCI-DSS compliance
sampleSqlQueries.code:
SELECT 
    payment_channel,
    COUNT(*) AS total_transactions,
    SUM(CASE WHEN transaction_amount IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS null_amounts,
    ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN transaction_amount IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS null_pct,
    AVG(processing_time_ms) AS avg_latency_ms
FROM redshift_db.payment_events_raw
WHERE transaction_timestamp >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '30 days'
GROUP BY payment_channel
HAVING null_pct > 0.5
ORDER BY total_transactions DESC;

sampleSqlQueries.title: AWS Glue PySpark ETL Data Cleansing Job (Amazon)
sampleSqlQueries.description: Automated PySpark transformation script for streaming data deduplication, anomaly tagging, and Parquet partitioning
sampleSqlQueries.code:
from awsglue.transforms import *
from awsglue.utils import getResolvedOptions
from pyspark.context import SparkContext
from awsglue.context import GlueContext
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, when, current_timestamp

glueContext = GlueContext(SparkContext.getOrCreate())
df = glueContext.create_dynamic_frame.from_catalog(
    database="payment_dw", 
    table_name="raw_fraud_stream"
).toDF()

# Data Quality Filter: Remove anomalies & cast types
cleaned_df = df.filter(col("amount") > 0) \
    .withColumn("is_anomalous", when(col("risk_score") > 0.85, True).otherwise(False)) \
    .withColumn("etl_processed_at", current_timestamp()) \
    .dropDuplicates(["transaction_id"])

cleaned_df.write.mode("append") \
    .partitionBy("payment_channel") \
    .parquet("s3://global-payments-analytics-prod/processed_transactions/")

caseStudies.title: Making agent-written SQL safe enough for enterprise data
metric: syntactic and relational accuracy on complex multi-table joins
caseStudies.context: Trida Labs builds AI-native analytics: AgentSQL turns plain-English questions into SQL and dashboards, and TridaPad is a collaborative data workspace. I deploy both into enterprise customers' own data stacks.
caseStudies.challenge: Non-technical stakeholders needed answers from data spread across PostgreSQL, Snowflake, Databricks and Redshift. SQL written by an LLM can hallucinate tables and joins on schemas like these, and multi-tenant customers need strict access control.
actions: Deployed and operationalised AgentSQL across enterprise customer architectures, so business users can generate production-grade SQL and dashboards from natural-language questions.
Built Model Context Protocol (MCP) server integrations that connect external LLMs and agent tools directly to customers' PostgreSQL, Snowflake, Databricks and Redshift databases.
Designed schema-aware prompt pipelines and deterministic SQL guardrails that keep generated queries inside the real schema.
Configured role-based access control and data-governance policies across multi-tenant cloud and on-prem deployments.
Brought edge-case query patterns and latency findings back to core product engineering, and tailored real-time collaboration workflows in TridaPad.
results: 99%+ syntactic and relational accuracy on complex multi-table joins
Business users generate SQL and dashboards on their own, in plain English
Compliance and security maintained across multi-tenant deployments
caseStudies.note: The 'Ask my twin' panel on this site shows the same pattern in miniature: allow-listed tables, key-equality joins, no cartesian products and row limits, checked before any query runs.
